title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan

epigraph.quote: The hardest discipline in investing is not finding things to buy; it is saying no to a great story when the cash flows and the price refuse to cooperate.
epigraph.author: Institutional Capital Allocation Rule

web_blocks.html:
Three-Horizon Independent Verdict:
• Short-Term Trading / Momentum (1–3 months): AVOID / REJECTED. Stage 4 breakdown below the 30-week SMA (₹431.16) and 50-DMA (₹451.06), 7 distribution days, and 816-share daily liquidity make this uninvestable for momentum.
• Medium-Term Inflection (6–12 months): REJECTED. Q2 FY27 D&A of ₹6.85 Cr/quarter is actively compressing net margins (₹0.21 Cr Q2 PAT), and the 118.89x P/E must digest heavy amortization.
• Long-Term Compounding (2–5 years): REJECTED (Watchlist Graduation Criteria Unmet). Eight years of negative FCF, 2.77% ROE, ₹90.22 Cr of capitalized intangibles, and 18.89% promoter ownership violate core compounder standards. Re-evaluation requires two consecutive quarters of positive FCF and contract assets falling below 120 days.

Current Portfolio Position & Redeployment Plan: Per the 13 November 2026 positions ledger, SOFTTECH is NOT HELD (0 shares; holding_action: NOT_HELD; holding_shares_to_sell: 0). Because no existing capital is tied up in SOFTTECH, the capital under review is the next marginal ₹1,00,000 of deployable cash. Rather than forcing capital into an overvalued Stage 4 micro-cap, we retain 100% in CASH while benchmarking two concrete alternatives: (1) MANORAMA from the active IN shortlist (CMP ₹1,984.10, Stage 2 BUY_AT_CMP_NO_FOMO, CLEAR_FOR_CONSIDERATION, Base Target ₹2,650.00, 2.12:1 R:R). This remains on standby for a dedicated underwriting ticket, and (2) NEWGEN as an outside software peer (CMP ₹439.15, 19.6x TTM P/E, 18.5% ROE, currently STAGE_4. keep at 0% until Stage 2 reclaim).

web_blocks.html: Decision Change Trigger: Re-underwrite SOFTTECH for new capital only when all four gates trigger together: (1) two consecutive quarters of positive FCF, (2) combined debtor plus unbilled days below 120, (3) D&A falling below 12% of sales, and (4) price reclaiming ₹455+ on >2x average volume.

book_paragraphs: We have reached the moment of truth. Let us put both sides of the SoftTech debate on the table without spin, without cheerleading, and without hiding behind vague 'wait for support' language.

First, give the bulls their due: Vijay Gupta built a genuine municipal software franchise across 1,500+ Indian cities, recurring SaaS revenue jumped 46.2% YoY in H1 FY27 to ₹28.21 Cr, and winning a ₹92.95 Cr AI Digital Twin contract at JNPA proves SoftTech can compete for marquee infrastructure projects. If you only read the investor presentation, you would think a multi-bagger is warming up in the bullpen.

Now face the forensic reality we uncovered before ever looking at the stock price. SoftTech has posted negative free cash flow for eight consecutive years. It carries ₹90.22 Cr of capitalized intangibles, more than half its net worth. And ₹53.52 Cr of unbilled contract assets. Worse, promoter ownership has been cut by more than half over three years to 18.89%, and the stock is priced at 118.89 times earnings while sitting in a Stage 4 breakdown on 816 shares of daily volume.

When we weight the three 12–18 month outcomes, 35% Bear at ₹225, 45% Base at ₹320, and 20% Bull at ₹500, the probability-weighted expected value is ₹322.75, or 24.3% below today's ₹425.90 price. Even if the stock dropped to its ₹373–₹384 support zone tomorrow, our Base Case of ₹320 would still be below the buy zone. Under our anti-hedging discipline, a setup with negative expected value at support cannot be dressed up as 'Wait for Support.' The honest, independent verdict is REJECTED.

Let us close by summarizing the exact four-gate checklist that would be required to ever bring SoftTech back onto our active watchlist. First, Free Cash Flow (operating cash flow minus all capex and capitalized software development) must turn positive for at least two consecutive quarters. Second, combined billed receivables and unbilled contract assets must compress below 120 days of revenue, proving that municipal and JNPA milestones convert cleanly into bank cash.

Third, quarterly depreciation must stabilize below 12% of revenue so that operating leverage actually reaches the bottom line instead of being absorbed by past R&D capitalization. Fourth, the stock must complete a Stage 1 base and reclaim ₹455+ on at least 2x average daily volume (8,500+ shares/day). Until those four objective milestones appear in audited filings and on the tape, our capital belongs in cash or in higher-quality Stage 2 compounders.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: What Would Make Us Change Our Mind?
book_callouts.text: Rejecting a stock is never personal—it is a conditional verdict on the current evidence and price. If SoftTech delivers two consecutive quarters of genuine positive free cash flow (CFO minus all capitalized software development > 0), brings combined receivables and unbilled contract assets below 120 days, and reclaims its 30-week SMA on 2x volume, we will gladly re-underwrite it from scratch.

book_subsections.title: Holding Action & Capital Redeployment
paragraphs: Because the 13 November 2026 positions ledger confirms we hold zero shares of SOFTTECH, there is nothing to trim or exit (NOT_HELD). For the next marginal ₹1,00,000 of new capital under review, our decision is to keep 100% in Cash rather than chasing a 119x P/E Stage 4 software micro-cap.

If you want software exposure in India, our outside benchmark Newgen Software trades at 19.6x TTM P/E with an 18.5% ROE, though it too is in Stage 4 and waits for trend repair. On the active shortlist, Stage 2 names like Manorama Industries (₹1,984.10, Base Target ₹2,650.00) already clear the technical gate and deserve priority in a dedicated buy review.
